summary: Rabbi Besser discusses the transition of generations in the desert and the story of Bilam in Parashat Balak. He explores the nature of leadership, the influence of money, and how Hashem uses obstacles to guide individuals toward good, even when their intentions are not initially aligned with His will.
questions: Why did Hashem change the instruction from hitting the rock to speaking to it?
What can we learn from the story of Honi HaMe'agel about answering the questions of a new generation?
How should we respond when someone insults us?
Can a person perform a good deed without intending to?
How can obstacles in our lives be interpreted as messages from Hashem?
